name: Fiongalla
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.

attributes.attribute: vowed not to sleep with a man

text: Fiongalla is an obscure Irish heroine linked with the province of Munster. The powerful woman druid Amerach came from Ulster, and she did not age as the years passed. She bewitched Fiongalla, the fair-cheeked one, and made her swear that she would not lie with any man until one delivered yew berries, holly boughs, plus marigolds. The hero Feargal performed this difficult task, and then Amerach's hold on Fiongalla was gone.

okr.objective: Fiongalla is a Munster heroine freed from a druid's spell.
key_results: Fiongalla is an Irish heroine linked with Munster.
The druid Amerach bewitched her and stayed ageless.
Amerach made her vow to remain celibate until a task was done.
The hero Feargal freed her by gathering three magical plants.
